title: Socratic checklist — living update & retirement (更新与退役)
rationale: A living systematic review needs explicit update mechanics before the first publication. Answers are recorded; the gate checks completeness. Sources are chapter/item-level references, not page numbers.

items.question: Is the update trigger defined in advance: which signals (new studies, changed conclusion, new intervention, search-alert hits) move the review from dormant to updating?
items.rationale: Ad-hoc updates drift into selective updating — the living-review analogue of selective reporting.
items.source: Cochrane Handbook v6 Ch.22 (prospective approaches to accumulating evidence); Elliott et al. 2017 (living systematic reviews, J Clin Epidemiol)
items.answer_format: trigger list with thresholds and the responsible actor

items.question: Is the search-alert mechanism configured and tested, with a verification that new records actually arrive?
items.rationale: An unverified alert is a false sense of currency; test it with a seeded record or a sentinel query.
items.source: Cochrane Handbook v6 Ch.22 (searching for updates)
items.answer_format: alert setup + last successful run + sentinel test result

items.question: Is the update cadence explicit (time-based, evidence-based, or hybrid) and documented with the last update date visible to readers?
items.rationale: Readers must know how stale a living review is; the date is part of the method.
items.source: Elliott et al. 2017 (living systematic reviews); Cochrane Handbook v6 Ch.22

items.question: Are the rules for when an update changes the conclusions (versus when new evidence is incorporated without changing them) precommitted?
items.rationale: Precommitted conclusion-change rules prevent confirmation-driven updating.
items.source: Cochrane Handbook v6 Ch.22; GRADE handbook (updating certainty)
items.answer_format: decision rule: what evidence change triggers a conclusion change

items.question: Is the versioning scheme for the review defined (version numbers, what changes per version, changelog format)?
items.rationale: A living document without versions cannot be cited or audited.
items.source: Elliott et al. 2017 (versioning of living reviews); Cochrane Handbook v6 Ch.22

items.question: Is the retirement rule explicit: under what conditions does the review stop updating (evidence stable, superseded, question obsolete)?
items.rationale: Living reviews must know how to die; otherwise the update burden is unbounded.
items.source: Elliott et al. 2017 (retiring living reviews); Cochrane Handbook v6 Ch.22

items.question: Does each update re-run the full reproducibility receipt (input freeze, code commit, environment, hashes) rather than patching in place?
items.rationale: An update is a new analysis; it inherits all reproducibility obligations of the original.
items.answer_format: new receipt per update + diff against the previous version

items.question: Are stage-gate obligations re-triggered by an update when the new evidence touches them (e.g., new studies trigger screening/extraction/appraisal gates)?
items.rationale: Updates that bypass stage gates silently degrade the review's assurance level.
items.source: MetaWingman stage-gated workflow; Cochrane Handbook v6 Ch.22
items.answer_format: per-stage re-trigger map: what new evidence re-opens which gate

items.question: Does the meta-update loop feed update observations back into the skill itself (new lessons, checklist revisions) with sources attached?
items.rationale: The living review and the living skill should improve together (lifelong-upgrades mechanism).
items.source: MetaWingman meta-update loop (audit log); ICLR 2026 lifelong-agents line
items.answer_format: lesson entries with sources + applied/unapplied status

items.question: Which update scenario would most stress the current mechanics, and has it been drilled once?
items.rationale: A one-off dry run of the hardest update (e.g., conclusion-changing new trial) exposes mechanics gaps cheaply.
